question: Does the remaining loss involve inconsistent mixture updates, finite-history cost of an added empirical prior, or source contexts that cannot distinguish target mechanisms before observations?
source_context: Compare the complete original local eta prior parameters and f/g selected functions for the four shared-source mechanisms at each seed48-55. Also compare their public initial8 candidate identities, separately from source parameters. Report actual equalities and differences; do not assert in advance that source contexts match. Mechanism and seed names are diagnostic indexing only.
accounting: For each of80 A43 paths at steps9-24, use cached U,I and empirical mass w. Reconstruct the pure empirical predictive density relative to I through exp(U-I)=1-w+w*exp(E-I). Check that post-observation empirical mass 1-(1-w)*exp(I-U) equals the next cached pre-observation mass. Check cumulative U-I=log((1-w9)/(1-w25)); its lower bound log(1-w9) describes only finite-history log predictive cost, not simulation calls or regret. Report all mechanisms, empirical-minus-local mean and past mass on worse empirical-density steps. Do not use the current label to select a model or change weights.
decision: A failed accounting identity requires fixing forecasts before interpreting scientific contrasts. Identical source contexts cannot justify a static mechanism-dependent prior gate; use paid target history for identification. Consistent finite-history mixing costs do not remove the failed source gate, prove optimality or justify a tuned mass. Preserve A43 and its negative evidence.
limitations: Accounting is exact for the cached approximation. Source-context identity shows a restriction on static context-only rules, not an impossibility of learning from target observations. This reused development cohort is not independent confirmation.
